reuse.why: Reuses getApproxNumberThreshold and getRangedAmount and collapses the five inline server dispatches into getExpectedAmount, but adds that function next to the existing getScheduledAmount instead of making the existing helper the single definition.

duplication.why: getScheduledAmount keeps its own null/range/number dispatch in parallel with getExpectedAmount, leaving two functions that both decide the expected amount.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts, and the server consumers and API model only call it.

scope.why: Only the amount rule, its consumers and the comments describing it.

maintainability.why: Two overlapping exported helpers with an optional op, plus desktop-client callers (Balance, schedule lists, edit hook) that call getScheduledAmount without op, so the planned amounts shown in the UI silently differ from server planning.

one_place.where: getExpectedAmount in packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts holds the rule for server paths, but getScheduledAmount keeps its own dispatch and the desktop-client callers (Balance.tsx, SchedulesTable.tsx, SchedulesListItem.tsx, MobileSchedulesPage.tsx) do not pass op, so they never apply the approximate rule
